_what_this_is: The fold model's fitted parameters. Written by scripts/calibrate-fold.mjs and read by supabase/functions/_shared/fold-preview.ts. It is DATA on purpose: calibrating is then a paste and a command, not a code change, and the basis travels with the numbers instead of living in a comment somebody has to find.
_why_it_exists_unfitted: A static import is the only form that reaches the hosted connector — an edge bundle carries the import graph and nothing else, which build-info.mjs learned the expensive way. So this file has to exist before it is fitted, and it says so rather than looking authoritative.
basis: NOT FITTED. Carried over from shape.ts, where FOLD_LINES, FOLD_CHARS_PER_LINE and FOLD_BLANK_COST are all flagged PROVISIONAL and have never been measured against any real render. Act on whether the hook lands above the cut; do not quote a character or word count as a measurement.

_notes_on_each_parameter.capacity: Line width, in the units of `widths`. With widths null this is literally characters per line, which is shape.ts's model.
_notes_on_each_parameter.blankCost: Rendered lines a blank source line costs. May be fractional: 0.5 means every other gap costs a line, which is real when paragraph spacing is under one line height. shape.ts floors this; fold-preview.ts does not.
_notes_on_each_parameter.seeMoreCost: Capacity consumed on the last visible line by the inline see-more link. Zero here because it has never been measured, and a guess would trade a known error for an unknown one.
_notes_on_each_parameter.breaksMidWord: Whether the renderer clips mid-word at the clamp point or backs up to a word boundary. CSS line-clamp does the former.
_notes_on_each_parameter.widths: Per-character relative advance, 1.0 being an average lowercase glyph. Null means a flat table, so every character is one unit — which cannot express that WWWWW is wider than iiiii, and is why a single capacity number can never be right for both.
